sources.title: Michael Vickery, Champa revised, ARI Working Paper 37 (2005)
sources.note: Direct PDF, printed pages 3 to 5 and 72 to 73. Multiple political centers and rival claims. Later corpus edition supersedes older inscription readings; speculative historical reconstructions not copied.

sources.title: Griffiths and Lepoutre, C.4: Doorjamb from Phan Rang, Corpus of the Inscriptions of Campā
sources.note: Direct scholarly edition, Old Cam, 1148 Śaka = 1226/7 CE; face A political events, face b lines 5 to 20 rice fields. Sample b9 and English translation directly checked. Latin transliteration, no invented original-script rendering.

sources.title: Griffiths and Lepoutre, C.30 B2: Po Nagar southern doorjamb
sources.note: Direct scholarly edition; revised thirteenth-century date, five Old Cam lines. English translation lists 55 enslaved people; Chinese identification explicitly uncertain and omitted here. Grouped with C4 as one corpus work for conservative budgets.

sources.title: Zhao Rugua, Chau Ju-kua: His Work on the Chinese and Arab Trade, translated by Hirth and Rockhill (1911)
sources.note: Downloaded public PDF and read printed pages 47 to 51, PDF indices 62 to 66. Text compiled around 1225, drawing on reports and older materials rather than a household census or direct fieldwork. Its editorial heading Annam refers here to Chan-cheng/Champa. Contradictory liquor assertions, inflated borders and supernatural claims excluded.

sources.title: Da Nang Tourism Promotion Center, Thap Mam Gallery
sources.note: Direct official account using museum labels/catalogues: twelfth/thirteenth-century complex, 1934 excavation and 58 tons of finds. Aesthetic decline judgment omitted.

sources.title: Da Nang Tourism Promotion Center, Dragon, BTC 222
sources.note: Direct official museum interpretation: twelfth-century sandstone dragon/makara, posture and gem. Dated as antecedent, not assigned an invented thirteenth-century date. Grouped with gallery as one museum guide work.

sources.title: William Southworth, Champa, The Oxford Handbook of Early Southeast Asia (2022)
sources.note: Indexed original scholarly abstract directly checked; full chapter not accessed. Its explicit limitation on post-fourth-century ceramic sequences supports cautious treatment of domestic archaeology, not universal absence of houses.

sources.title: Kathlene Baldanza, A brief history of Annan, Ming China and Vietnam (2016)
sources.note: Direct chapter, Displaced by the Mongol wars, printed page 21 onward: 1283 demand for passage and supplies, Tran refusal, following campaigns. Used only to establish continuing polity after atlas endpoint and regional diplomacy.

sources.title: UNESCO, Art of pottery-making of Chăm people, inscription 2022
sources.note: Original institutional description of living practice: women rotate around pots, family teaching, outdoor firing seven/eight hours about 800°C. Modern evidence explicitly not projected into 1200.

proposedOverrides.name: Champa City States
proposedOverrides.summary: Thirteenth-century Cham coastal powers, temple estates and maritime commerce, with multiple centers and continuing communities.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact 1200 to 1279 indexed record only. Separate period-specific narrative; do not alias the existing broad champa card, or Khmer, Dai Viet and modern Vietnam. The imported alias Champa alone is insufficient to share all content.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded sole world-1200 feature. Bounding box 106.4513,10.3487 to109.3061,16.6915. My Son, Tra Kieu, Vijaya and Phan Rang included; tested Po Nagar and Nhan Tower points omitted. Public overview makes coastal omissions and uncertain borders explicit. No repaired geometry supplied.
batchIdentityNotes.dates: All core political, epigraphic and trade evidence is thirteenth century. Twelfth-century dragon is explicitly antecedent; 1934/2011 excavations, 2022 archaeology overview and modern pottery are separately dated. No invented midpoint years. The later 1283 campaign demonstrates continuity after the atlas interval.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: C4 face b9: humā parik· 155 jāk·, exact scholarly Latin transliteration and matching English translation. Dated1148 Śaka/1226 to 1227 CE at Phan Rang. No fabricated Unicode Cham rendering; jāk not converted to modern acreage.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Zhao’s report blends sources and includes errors, legends and generalizations; passages expressly attributed, omitting magical trials, punishment sensationalism, contradicted liquor claims and obsolete geography. C30B2 uses revised corpus thirteenth-century chronology. Museum matriarchy and artistic decline generalizations excluded. Modern pottery does not establish medieval family structure. No supported historic medical treatment or toilet reconstruction established here.
batchIdentityNotes.budget: Group C4 and C30B2 as one corpus; museum gallery and dragon as one guide work; whole Zhao volume as one work. Check all runtime sources and URL/DOI aliases before freezing.
